cases.name: started-line-at-write-time
cases.detail: `ATM_IDENTITY=fx-at9-beta ATM_TEAM=fx-at9 atm task start at9-c1-1792636449 --json` -> {"action":"send","sender":"fx-at9-beta","outcome":"sent","message_id":"01M5GQB4F82HZ1KFZ6X24TF2PX","task_id":"at9-c1-1792636449","summary":"started at9-c1-1792636449"}. This was before alpha's read. Alpha's `atm list --unread --json` then showed rows[0] {"message_id":"01M5GQB4F82HZ1KFZ6X24TF2PX","summary":"started at9-c1-1792636449","from":"fx-at9-beta","read":false,"task_id":"at9-c1-1792636449"}. `atm read --message-id 01M5GQB4F82HZ1KFZ6X24TF2PX --json` -> "taskId":"at9-c1-1792636449","taskOp":{"op":"start"}. `atm task events at9-c1-1792636449 --json` -> events[].event 'started' (seq 3, to_state active) and handoffs[].kind 'task_started' (agent fx-at9-alpha, at 2026-10-22T02:34:17.448Z). Note: `--as` on `atm task assign` returned 'identity is not configured', so the ATM_IDENTITY/ATM_TEAM env prefix was used for all task commands.

cases.name: out-of-order-start-reorders-queue
cases.detail: Assigned at9-c2a-1792636449 then at9-c2b-1792636449 (each returned {"task_id":...}); beta ran `atm task start at9-c2b-1792636449 --json` (summary 'started at9-c2b-1792636449'). `atm task list --json` as beta -> [{"task_id":"at9-c2b-1792636449","state":"active","position":1,...},{"task_id":"at9-c2a-1792636449","state":"assigned","position":2,...}]

cases.name: unstarted-task-keeps-reminding
cases.detail: Assigned at9-c3-1792636449 at 02:34:23Z (`{"task_id":"at9-c3-1792636449"}`) and did not start it. `atm task events at9-c3-1792636449 --json` handoffs[] contained {"kind":"task_reminder","attempt":1,"at":"2026-10-22T02:35:25.580718217Z","task_id":"at9-c3-1792636449","trigger":"task_pass"} and {"kind":"task_reminder","attempt":2,"at":"2026-10-22T02:36:25.581296615Z","task_id":"at9-c3-1792636449","trigger":"task_pass"}, seen at 02:36:28Z (125s after assign, inside the 150s limit). The first 'reminded' event and the 'task_ready' handoff (02:34:25Z) were not counted. `atm task list --json` as beta -> "state":"assigned","position":1.

cases.name: cleanup
cases.detail: `atm task close <id> <outcome> <reason> --json` returned outcome 'sent' for at9-c1-1792636449 (completed, summary 'done'), at9-c2b-1792636449 (completed, 'done'), at9-c2a-1792636449 (cancelled, 'cleanup') and at9-c3-1792636449 (cancelled, 'cleanup'), each with rc=0. Final `atm task list --json` as beta -> []
